symbols.name: \vec E
symbols.def: \(\vec E\) contains one fixed orientation of every undirected ratio-restriction edge.

symbols.name: \mathcal C_G
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_G\) is the set of connected components of the undirected graph induced by \(\vec E\).

symbols.name: P_{\mathrm{obs}}
symbols.role: Joint law of observed setting-indexed outcomes, treatments, and controls.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: \(X\) collects all observed controls used in the setting-specific short regressions.
symbols.role: Observed adjustment variables retained unchanged by the attainment construction.

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: \(D=(D_1,\ldots,D_K)\) is the vector of centered treatments after partialling out observed controls under \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).
symbols.role: Residualized treatments retained unchanged by the attainment construction.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: \(Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_K)\) is the vector of centered outcomes after partialling out observed controls under \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).
symbols.role: Residualized outcomes retained unchanged by the attainment construction.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: \(s=(s_1,\ldots,s_K)\) is the vector of population short-regression coefficients under \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

symbols.name: \nu^-
symbols.def:
\(
u^-=(
u^-_1,\ldots,
u^-_K)\) is the vector of lower OVB limits.

symbols.name: \nu^+
symbols.def:
\(
u^+=(
u^+_1,\ldots,
u^+_K)\) is the vector of upper OVB limits.

symbols.name: P
symbols.role: Law including latent controls and setting-specific structural equations.

symbols.name: \theta(P)
symbols.def: \(\theta(P)=(\theta_1(P),\ldots,\theta_K(P))\) is the vector of long-regression causal coefficients.

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: \(Z\sim N(0,I_K)\) is drawn independently of the entire observed vector when forming the augmented law.
symbols.role: Latent-control randomizer used only on zero-bias coordinates.

symbols.name: \rho(P)
symbols.def: \(\rho(P)=(\rho_{jk}(P))_{(j,k)\in\vec E}\) is a witness to the cross-setting proportional-bias restrictions.

symbols.name: \mathcal M_{\mathrm{HK}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
symbols.role: Project-maintained generalized positive-ratio OVB class, reducing to the published class when every interval contains one.

symbols.name: \Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
symbols.role: Sharp identified set for the causal effect vector.

symbols.name: P^B
symbols.def: \(P^B\) is the joint law obtained by augmenting the unchanged observed draw with \(A^B\) for a feasible vector \(B\in\mathcal B_G\).

symbols.name: z
symbols.def: \(z_c\) selects the nonnegative branch when \(z_c=1\) and the nonpositive branch when \(z_c=0\).

symbols.name: \Theta_I(H,t)
symbols.role: Sharp effect set after simultaneous pins.

symbols.name: H_3
symbols.role: Simultaneous first- and third-effect pin matrix.

symbols.name: t_3
symbols.role: Simultaneous pin values for the worked instance.

symbols.name: p
symbols.role: Dimension of the observed primitive-moment vector.

symbols.name: O_{nr}
symbols.def: \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) are the observations in row \(n\) of the triangular array.

symbols.name: h(O)
symbols.def: \(h(O)\) collects undivided regression cross-products and bias-bound calibration moments.

symbols.name: \Gamma
symbols.def: \(\Gamma(\mu)=(s(\mu),\nu^-(\mu),\nu^+(\mu),d(\mu))\), where \(d_i(\mu)\) is the undivided short-minus-supershort coefficient change in setting \(i\).

symbols.name: P_0

symbols.name: \psi_q(\mu)

symbols.name: e_m

assumptions.condition: For every \(i\in V\), the full law \(P\) admits \(Y_i=\theta_i(P)D_i+f_i(X_i,A_i)+\varepsilon_i\) with \(E_P[\varepsilon_i\mid D_i,X_i,A_i]=0\) and a positive residual variance for \(D_i\) after projection on \((X_i,A_i)\).
For every \((j,k)\in\vec E\), \(0<\ell_{jk}\le u_{jk}\) and there exists \(\rho_{jk}(P)\in[\ell_{jk},u_{jk}]\) such that \(B_j(P)=\rho_{jk}(P)B_k(P)\).

novel.justification: Positive proportional biases with pair-specific intervals that need not contain one accommodate calibrated settings whose relative confounding direction is common but whose magnitudes are known to be ordered, as when administrative sites share an omitted risk index and external validation bounds one site's loading above another's.

assumptions.condition: Under \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), conditional on \(X\), the residualized vector \((D^\top,U^\top)^\top\) has a jointly Gaussian distribution that does not depend on \(X\), has a positive-definite covariance matrix, satisfies \(\operatorname{Var}(D_i)=1\), and satisfies \(\operatorname{Cov}(D_i,U_i)=0\) for every \(i\in V\); cross-setting covariances are unrestricted subject to positive definiteness.
For each \(n\), \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P_n\).
There exist fixed \(\delta>0\) and \(C<\infty\) such that \(\sup_n E_{P_n}[\|h(O_{n1})-\mu_n\|^{4+\delta}]\le C\).
There exist fixed \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that every eigenvalue of \(\Omega_n\) lies in \([c,C]\).
The map \(\Gamma\) is continuously differentiable with uniformly bounded derivative on a fixed neighborhood of \(\{\mu_n:n\ge1\}\).

standard.name: Regular finite-dimensional moment transformation away from regression singularity

definitions.name: Generalized Huntington--Klein compatible-law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{HK}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{P:\text{ass:partially-linear-model, ass:observational-equivalence, ass:bias-box, and ass:positive-ratio hold for }(K,V,\vec E,s,\nu^-,\nu^+,\ell,u,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}\).

definitions.name: Sharp multi-setting effect set
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{\theta(P):P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{HK}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}\).

definitions.name: Positive bias branch
definitions.construction: For \(c\in\mathcal C_G\), \(\mathcal P_c^+=\{b_c\in\mathbb R^c:\nu^-_i\le b_i\le\nu^+_i,\ b_i\ge0\ \forall i\in c,\ \ell_{jk}b_k\le b_j\le u_{jk}b_k\ \forall(j,k)\in\vec E\cap(c\times c)\}\).

definitions.name: Negative bias branch
definitions.construction: For \(c\in\mathcal C_G\), \(\mathcal P_c^-=\{b_c\in\mathbb R^c:\nu^-_i\le b_i\le\nu^+_i,\ b_i\le0\ \forall i\in c,\ u_{jk}b_k\le b_j\le\ell_{jk}b_k\ \forall(j,k)\in\vec E\cap(c\times c)\}\).

definitions.name: Componentwise sharp bias union
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_G=\prod_{c\in\mathcal C_G}(\mathcal P_c^+\cup\mathcal P_c^-)\subseteq\mathbb R^K\).

definitions.name: Bias-difference outer polytope
definitions.construction:
Let \(c^-_{jk}=\min\{(r-1)v:r\in\{\ell_{jk},u_{jk}\},\ v\in\{
u^-_k,
u^+_k\}\}\) and define \(c^+_{jk}\) by replacing \(\min\) with \(\max\). Then \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{HK}}=\{\vartheta\in\mathbb R^K:s_i-
u^+_i\le\vartheta_i\le s_i-
u^-_i,\ (s_j-s_k)-c^+_{jk}\le\vartheta_j-\vartheta_k\le(s_j-s_k)-c^-_{jk}\  orall(j,k)\in\vec E\}\).

definitions.name: Gaussian attainment subclass
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_G(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{P:\text{ass:partially-linear-model, ass:observational-equivalence, ass:bias-box, ass:positive-ratio, and ass:gaussian-observed-submodel hold for }(K,V,\vec E,s,\nu^-,\nu^+,\ell,u,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}\).

definitions.name: Joint-margin-preserving Gaussian latent-control completion
definitions.construction: For \(B\in\mathcal B_G\), start with one draw of the entire observed vector from \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), retain all its coordinates unchanged, compute \(U_i=Y_i-s_iD_i\), and independently draw \(Z\sim N(0,I_K)\). Define \(A_i^B=D_i+U_i/B_i\) and \(\varepsilon_i^B=0\) when \(B_i\ne0\); define \(A_i^B=Z_i\) and \(\varepsilon_i^B=U_i\) when \(B_i=0\). Set \(\theta_i^B=s_i-B_i\) and \(f_i^B(A_i^B)=B_iA_i^B\), adding back the observed-control projection to \(f_i^B\) when lifting the residualized equation. The augmented joint law of the unchanged observed vector and \(A^B\) is \(P^B\), and its residualized structural equation is \(Y_i=\theta_i^BD_i+f_i^B(A_i^B)+\varepsilon_i^B\).

definitions.name: Closure-complete log-difference system
definitions.construction: For component \(c\) and sign \(\zeta\in\{+,-\}\), the nonzero stratum uses \(x_i=\log|b_i|\). Each ratio edge contributes \(x_j-x_k\le\log u_{jk}\) and \(x_k-x_j\le-\log\ell_{jk}\); the sign-adjusted box contributes the finite log lower and upper bounds that exist. These inequalities form \(\mathcal D_c^{\zeta}\). Add a separate all-zero stratum exactly when \(0\in[\nu^-_i,\nu^+_i]\) for every \(i\in c\).

definitions.name: Exact branch linear programs
definitions.construction: For every sign map \(\zeta:\mathcal C_G\to\{+,-\}\), minimize and maximize \(q^\top(s-b)\) subject to \(b_c\in\mathcal P_c^{\zeta(c)}\) for all \(c\), and, when pins are requested, \(H(s-b)=t\). Discard infeasible branches and take the extrema over the remaining branches.

definitions.name: Exact disjunctive MILP
definitions.construction:
Let \(M\in[0,\infty)^K\) have \(M_i=\max\{|
u_i^-|,|
u_i^+|\}\), and let \(M_{jk}=(1+u_{jk})\max\{M_j,M_k\}\ge0\). Use \(b\in[
u^-,
u^+]\), \(z_c\in\{0,1\}\), and \(-M_i(1-z_c)\le b_i\le M_i z_c\) for \(i\in c\). For \((j,k)\in\vec E\cap(c	imes c)\), impose \(\ell_{jk}b_k-M_{jk}(1-z_c)\le b_j\le u_{jk}b_k+M_{jk}(1-z_c)\) and \(u_{jk}b_k-M_{jk}z_c\le b_j\le\ell_{jk}b_k+M_{jk}z_c\). Optimize \(q^	op(s-b)\) and add \(H(s-b)=t\) when pins are requested.

definitions.name: Sharp simultaneous pin slice
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_I(H,t)=\{s-b:b\in\mathcal B_G,\ H(s-b)=t\}\).

definitions.name: Relaxation support gap
definitions.construction: \(\Delta(q)=h_{\mathcal J_{\mathrm{HK}}}(q)-h_{s-\mathcal B_G}(q)\).

definitions.name: Total regularized primitive-moment Wald set
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal U_n=\{\mu\in\mathbb R^p:n(\bar h_n-\mu)^\top\widetilde\Omega_n^{-1}(\bar h_n-\mu)\le\chi^2_{p,1-\alpha}\}\), where \(\widetilde\Omega_n=\widehat\Omega_n+\lambda_n I_p\) is positive definite on every sample.

definitions.name: Undivided supershort component branch
definitions.construction: For \(c\in\mathcal C_G\) and \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\), \(\mathcal B_{c,\sigma}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)=\{b_c\in\mathbb R^c:\nu_i^-(\mu)\le b_i\le\nu_i^+(\mu),\ \sigma b_i\ge0\ \forall i\in c,\ d_j(\mu)d_k(\mu)\ge0,\ Q_{jk}(b,\mu)\le0\ \forall(j,k)\in\vec E\cap(c\times c)\}\).

definitions.name: Componentwise undivided supershort bias union
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)=\prod_{c\in\mathcal C_G}\bigl(\mathcal B_{c,+1}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\cup\mathcal B_{c,-1}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\bigr)\).

definitions.name: Supershort-calibrated sensitivity region
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)=\{s(\mu)-b:b\in\mathcal B_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\}\).

definitions.name: Directional endpoint map
definitions.construction: For fixed \(q\in\mathbb R^K\), define \(\psi_q(\mu)=(\underline\psi_q(\mu),\overline\psi_q(\mu))\), where \(\underline\psi_q(\mu)=\inf_{\theta\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)}q^\top\theta\) and \(\overline\psi_q(\mu)=\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)}q^\top\theta\).

definitions.name: Hong--Li finite-perturbation endpoint Jacobian
definitions.construction: For \(m\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\), define the \(m\)-th column by \(\widehat J_{q,n}^{(m)}=\{\psi_q(\bar h_n+\varepsilon_n e_m)-\psi_q(\bar h_n)\}/\varepsilon_n\).

definitions.name: Numerical-delta and known-cell oracle endpoint intervals
definitions.construction: For endpoint coordinate \(r\in\{1,2\}\), let \(v_{r,n}^{\mathrm{ND}}=[\widehat J_{q,n}\widetilde\Omega_n\widehat J_{q,n}^\top]_{rr}\) and \(v_{r,n}^{\mathrm{or}}=[J_q(\bar h_n)\widetilde\Omega_nJ_q(\bar h_n)^\top]_{rr}\). The \(r\)-th members of \(\mathcal I_{q,n}^{\mathrm{ND}}\) and \(\mathcal I_{q,n}^{\mathrm{or}}\) are respectively \(\psi_{q,r}(\bar h_n)\pm\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\sqrt{v_{r,n}^{\mathrm{ND}}/n}\) and \(\psi_{q,r}(\bar h_n)\pm\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\sqrt{v_{r,n}^{\mathrm{or}}/n}\), where \(\Phi\) is the standard-normal distribution function.

definitions.name: Singularity-robust confidence region
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{inv}}=\bigcup_{\mu\in\mathcal U_n}\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\), computed by sign-component enumeration and globally certified quadratic feasibility without forming any ratio \(d_j(\mu)/d_k(\mu)\).

definitions.name: Adaptive singularity-to-oracle handle
definitions.construction: Design \(\mathsf H_n\) by combining the undivided confidence region \(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{inv}}\) on data-detected neighborhoods of zero coefficient changes or vanishing branch and basis margins with the numerical-delta intervals \(\mathcal I_{q,n}^{\mathrm{ND}}\) on separated regular cells; determine the switching thresholds from simultaneous \(\widetilde\Omega_n\)-studentized primitive-moment, ratio-order, branch-margin, slack, and reduced-cost tests.

statements.statement: A vector \(b\in\prod_{i\in V}[\nu^-_i,\nu^+_i]\) admits edge witnesses \(r_{jk}\in[\ell_{jk},u_{jk}]\) with \(b_j=r_{jk}b_k\) for all \((j,k)\in\vec E\) if and only if \(b\in\mathcal B_G\). In a connected component, either every coordinate is zero or every nonzero coordinate has one common sign; sign choices are independent across distinct components.
statements.justification: This is the exact closure step discarded by separate bias-difference extrema.
statements.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026 notes common signs and transitivity but does not state the componentwise if-and-only-if union, especially at zero.
statements.consumer: It determines the correct feasible region and reduces sign enumeration from one bit per setting or edge to one bit per connected component.

statements.statement: For every \(B\in\mathcal B_G\), the law \(P^B\) from def:gaussian-completion has observed margin exactly \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), including every cross-setting covariance, satisfies the partially linear model, has \(B(P^B)=B\), belongs to \(\mathcal M_G(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{HK}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), and yields \(\theta(P^B)=s-B\). Coordinatewise, if \(B_i\ne0\), then \((s_i-B_i)D_i+B_i(D_i+U_i/B_i)=s_iD_i+U_i=Y_i\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(D_i\mid X,A_i^B)=\operatorname{Var}(U_i)/(B_i^2+\operatorname{Var}(U_i))>0\); if \(B_i=0\), then \(s_iD_i+U_i=Y_i\), \(E[U_i\mid D_i,X,Z_i]=0\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(D_i\mid X,Z_i)=1\).
statements.justification: A sharpness claim needs one observationally equivalent latent-confounder completion for every feasible bias vector.
statements.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026 proves containment algebraically and gives no reverse construction; BalkePearl1997 supplies the methodological standard for attainment but not this model.
statements.consumer: It makes the union sharp over a nondegenerate jointly Gaussian observed-law family while preserving arbitrary observed dependence across settings.

statements.statement: For every observed law, \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq s-\mathcal B_G\subseteq\mathcal J_{\mathrm{HK}}\). Under ass:gaussian-observed-submodel, \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=s-\mathcal B_G\), so the affine componentwise sign union is pointwise sharp throughout the stated nonsingular jointly Gaussian observed-law family, without restricting cross-setting covariances.
statements.justification: This replaces a merely valid polytope by the sharp multi-setting causal effect set.
statements.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026, Proposition 4 on p. 13, proves only membership in \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{HK}}\); it does not enforce one componentwise same-sign ratio-compatible vector or prove converse attainability.
statements.consumer: Every marginal bound, effect contrast, and joint heterogeneity claim computed by the released software can be re-evaluated against the exact set.

statements.statement:
For every component \(c\) and sign \(\zeta\), the nonzero branch \(\mathcal P_c^{\zeta}\) is nonempty if and only if the directed difference system \(\mathcal D_c^{\zeta}\) has no negative-weight directed cycle, equivalently if and only if no nonnegative Farkas circulation \(y\) satisfies \(y^	op A=0\) and \(y^	op b<0\). Together with the separately tested all-zero stratum, these certificates are closure-complete. For every \((q,H,t)\), exhaustive branch LP and def:exact-milp have exactly the feasible set \(\Theta_I(H,t)\) and identical attained extrema, including equality cycles and optimizer ties. If \(M_i=0\), the box and sign constraints force \(b_i=0\), and every active positive-ratio edge incident to \(i\) propagates zero throughout its connected component. In the exact rational check \(K=2\), \([
u^-_1,
u^+_1]=\{0\}\), \([
u^-_2,
u^+_2]=[-1,1]\), and \([\ell_{12},u_{12}]=[1/2,2]\), both the branch-LP bias projection and the MILP bias projection equal \(\{(0,0)\}\), with \(M_1=0\), \(M_2=1\), and \(M_{12}=3\).
statements.justification: Exact identification is useful only if infeasibility and boundary cases have short verifiable certificates and the optimization backend preserves the set.
statements.gap: KitamuraStoye2018 gives primal and dual cone representations for random utility, while HuntingtonKlein2026 uses pairwise LP constraints; neither treats the sign-union and zero-stratum ratio graph.
statements.consumer: R, Python, and Stata implementations can return a violated cycle or Farkas multiplier instead of a tolerance-dependent empty-set message.

statements.statement:
Let \(K=2\), \(
u^-_1=
u^-_2=-a\), \(
u^+_1=
u^+_2=a\), \(\ell_{12}=1/R\), and \(u_{12}=R\), with \(a>0\) and \(R>1\). Then \(s-\mathcal B_G\subsetneq\mathcal J_{\mathrm{HK}}\) and the effect-difference support gap is \(\Delta(q_{12})=a\{\min(2,R-1)-(1-R^{-1})\}>0\). Hence strictness holds over the full nondegenerate parameter region \(a>0,R>1\), not at one tuned law.
statements.justification: A closed-form support loss establishes economically material non-sharpness beyond a single counterexample.
statements.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026 supplies a symmetric worked example but does not compare its polytope with the primitive ratio set or quantify a relaxation gap.
statements.consumer: Users can measure how much an outer-polytope heterogeneity conclusion is driven solely by discarded sign compatibility.

statements.statement: For arbitrary \((H,t)\), the sharp pinned set is exactly \(\Theta_I(H,t)\), its support endpoints are the extrema over the feasible branch LPs, and branchwise primal--dual alternatives classify each requested pin system as infeasible, redundant, or jointly binding. In the family of thm:strict-support-relaxation-gap with \(R=2\), pinning \(\theta_1=s_1-a\) yields the sharp slice \(\theta_2\in[s_2-a,s_2-a/2]\), whereas slicing the outer set as in HuntingtonKlein2026, Definition 3 on p. 15, yields \(\theta_2\in[s_2-a,s_2]\); the requested-pin upper-endpoint gap is exactly \(a/2\).
statements.justification: Pinning is the anchor paper's main device for interpreting joint heterogeneity, so its slices must share one attainable bias witness.
statements.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026, Definition 3 on p. 15, slices the outer difference polytope and does not characterize simultaneous sharp pins or quantify their endpoint error.
statements.consumer: The ACS returns-to-college analysis can distinguish an effect configuration ruled out by the common bias mechanism from one merely removed by a marginal pin.

statements.statement: In \(\mathcal W_3\), \(\mathcal B_G\) equals \(\{(x,y,x):0\le x\le a,\ x/2\le y\le\min\{2x,a\}\}\cup\{(x,y,x):-a\le x\le0,\ \max\{2x,-a\}\le y\le x/2\}\). Its zero stratum is the singleton \(\{(0,0,0)\}\). On either nonzero sign branch, the log system contains the equality-cycle inequalities \(x_3-x_1\le0\) and \(x_1-x_3\le0\), whose zero-weight directed cycle certifies \(x_1=x_3\), and every remaining directed cycle has nonnegative weight. With simultaneous pins \(H_3\theta=t_3\), the sharp slice is \(\{(s_1-a,\theta_2,s_3-a):\theta_2\in[s_2-a,s_2-a/2]\}\), while the corresponding \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{HK}}\) slice replaces that interval by \([s_2-a,s_2]\); its upper-endpoint relaxation gap is exactly \(a/2\).
statements.justification: One solved cycle exposes the equality-cycle certificate, the zero closure face, and the simultaneous-pin loss in the published outer geometry without relying on software output.
statements.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026, Proposition 4 on p. 13 and Definition 3 on p. 15, do not solve a three-setting equality cycle or quantify the gap after two effects are pinned simultaneously.
statements.consumer: The worked instance is an exact regression test for the R, Python, and Stata solvers and a template for the ACS multi-state pinning analysis.

statements.statement: Fix \((j,k)\in\vec E\) and a branch with \(b_jb_k\ge0\). If \(d_j(\mu)d_k(\mu)>0\), then \(Q_{jk}(b,\mu)\le0\) holds if and only if either \(b_j=b_k=0\), or \(b_jb_k>0\) and \(b_j/b_k\) lies between the two positive reciprocal calibration ratios \(d_j(\mu)/d_k(\mu)\) and \(d_k(\mu)/d_j(\mu)\). If exactly one of \(d_j(\mu)\) and \(d_k(\mu)\) is zero, then \(Q_{jk}(b,\mu)=-b_jb_kd_m(\mu)^2\le0\), where \(m\) indexes the nonzero coordinate. If both are zero, then \(Q_{jk}(b,\mu)=0\).
statements.justification: The exhaustive zero-case identity gives a total polynomial replacement for divided calibration ratios on every component branch.
statements.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026, Assumption 4 on pp. 17--18, uses conditional divided supershort ratios; it does not state this project-maintained polynomial generalization or its exact zero-coordinate cases.
statements.consumer: The inference routine can evaluate every null at zero or local-to-zero coefficient changes without arbitrary clipping.

statements.statement: For fixed \(p\), every deterministic \(\lambda_n>0\) with \(\lambda_n\downarrow0\), and every \(\varepsilon>0\), the admissible triangular arrays satisfy \(\sup_{(P_n)}P_n\{\|\widehat\Omega_n-\Omega_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon\}\to0\), \(\widetilde\Omega_n\succ0\) on every sample, and \(\sup_{(P_n)}P_n\bigl(\bigl|n(\bar h_n-\mu_n)^\top\widetilde\Omega_n^{-1}(\bar h_n-\mu_n)-n(\bar h_n-\mu_n)^\top\Omega_n^{-1}(\bar h_n-\mu_n)\bigr|>\varepsilon\bigr)\to0\).
statements.justification: Regularization makes inversion total while uniform covariance consistency guarantees that it does not alter the first-order pivotal quadratic form.
statements.gap: KaidoMolinariStoye2019 uses regular estimated covariance matrices in calibrated projection; it does not establish the finite-sample totalization and uniform Slutsky equivalence needed for this primitive inversion.
statements.consumer: The confidence-region implementation can return a defined answer even when a finite sample has collinear or duplicate primitive moments.

statements.statement: For every sample, the deterministic event inclusion \(\{\mu_n\in\mathcal U_n\}\subseteq\{\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu_n)\subseteq\bigcup_{\mu\in\mathcal U_n}\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\}\) holds by set inclusion, and the union on the right is \(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{inv}}\). Under ass:iid-triangular-sampling, ass:primitive-moment-envelope, and ass:primitive-covariance, for fixed \(p\) and \(K\), the fixed-dimensional triangular-array central limit theorem, uniform covariance consistency, and regularized Slutsky equivalence give \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P_n)}P_n\{\mu_n\in\mathcal U_n\}\ge1-\alpha\), and therefore \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P_n)}P_n\{\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu_n)\subseteq\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{inv}}\}\ge1-\alpha\). This supporting coverage guarantee is uniform over exact-zero and \(n^{-1/2}\)-weak coordinates of \(d(\mu_n)\), component-sign ties, and branch or optimizer-basis ties; it requires no divided-ratio or endpoint-optimizer limit law.
statements.justification: This supporting lemma records that all probabilistic work is primitive-ellipsoid coverage, while the image-set inclusion itself is deterministic.
statements.gap: KaidoMolinariStoye2019 supplies the general projection-inference template; the role here is to totalize its primitive covariance step and record honest coverage for the project-specific undivided union, not to claim union inversion as a new inference principle.
statements.consumer: Empirical users receive one confidence set valid for the ACS application even when a state's observed coefficient change is indistinguishable from zero.

statements.statement: Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^K\) and a fixed admissible law \(P_0\), viewed as the constant sequence \(P_n=P_0\), with \(\mu_n=\mu_0\) and \(\Omega_n=\Omega_0\). Suppose ass:iid-triangular-sampling, ass:primitive-moment-envelope, ass:primitive-covariance, and ass:regular-primitive-map hold; \(d_i(\mu_0)\ne0\) for every \(i\in V\); \(d_j(\mu_0)^2-d_k(\mu_0)^2\ne0\) for every \((j,k)\in\vec E\); the lower and upper endpoint problems defining \(\psi_q(\mu_0)\) have uniquely winning component-sign branches and unique primal--dual bases; and their branch-selection, primal-slack, dual-slack, and reduced-cost margins are strictly positive. Then a neighborhood of \(\mu_0\) has the same ratio ordering, winning branches, and primal--dual bases, and \(\psi_q\) is continuously differentiable there by the active-basis or KKT formula composed with \(\Gamma\). Consequently, \(\sqrt n\{\psi_q(\bar h_n)-\psi_q(\mu_0)\}=J_q(\mu_0)\sqrt n(\bar h_n-\mu_0)+o_{P_0}(1)\Rightarrow N(0,J_q(\mu_0)\Omega_0J_q(\mu_0)^\top)\). For every \(\varepsilon_n\downarrow0\) with \(\sqrt n\,\varepsilon_n\to\infty\), \(\widehat J_{q,n}\to_{P_0}J_q(\mu_0)\). If both diagonal entries of \(J_q(\mu_0)\Omega_0J_q(\mu_0)^\top\) are positive, each lower or upper endpoint of \(\mathcal I_{q,n}^{\mathrm{ND}}\) differs from its corresponding known-cell oracle endpoint in \(\mathcal I_{q,n}^{\mathrm{or}}\) by \(o_{P_0}(n^{-1/2})\). This conclusion is pointwise at \(P_0\).
statements.justification: Strict branch and basis margins turn the apparently nonsmooth endpoint problem into one stable differentiable cell and certify first-order oracle behavior there.
statements.gap: HongLi2018 establishes numerical-delta validity for directionally differentiable maps, while FangSantos2019 characterizes bootstrap behavior at nondifferentiable maps; neither derives the fixed-cell Jacobian, basis-stability neighborhood, and oracle-equivalent endpoint intervals for this componentwise supershort union.
statements.consumer: In regular ACS specifications, software can report short Gaussian endpoint intervals with a theorem identifying exactly when they coincide to first order with a known-branch, known-basis oracle.

statements.statement: Can one construct \(\mathsf H_n\) from def:hybrid-handle and derive data-dependent switching thresholds such that one data-dependent confidence procedure has the uniform coverage guarantee of lem:uniform-primitive-inversion over exact-zero, \(n^{-1/2}\)-weak, branch-tie, and basis-tie sequences, while at every fixed regular law satisfying the strict-cell conditions of thm:pointwise-regular-cell-oracle-recovery its endpoints differ from \(\mathcal I_{q,n}^{\mathrm{or}}\) by \(o_p(n^{-1/2})\)?
statements.justification: Uniform validity alone can be conservative; the unresolved theorem is whether one procedure can also recover oracle precision whenever the singularities are separated.
statements.gap: HongLi2018 gives numerical-delta inference for directional maps, and AndrewsMikusheva2016 combines weak-identification validity with strong-identification efficiency in Gaussian moments, but neither covers a data-dependent transition for a discontinuous supershort-calibrated union of LP values.
statements.consumer: Software can default to a single honest procedure rather than forcing practitioners to choose ex ante between a wide robust region and a fragile regular approximation.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling within each row of a fixed-dimensional triangular array.
sampling_model.units: \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\sim P_n\), with setting indicators and the observations required for short and supershort regressions.
sampling_model.treatment: Each setting has a real-valued treatment entering the partially linear causal coefficient \(\theta_i(P_n)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The residual treatment variances used by the regular map \(\Gamma\) are uniformly positive; no positivity condition is imposed on any supershort coefficient change \(d_i(\mu_n)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate the undivided primitive moment \(\mu_n\) by \(\bar h_n\), form \(\widetilde\Omega_n=\widehat\Omega_n+\lambda_n I_p\) with deterministic \(\lambda_n\downarrow0\), and map every accepted primitive vector through the componentwise polynomial sensitivity solver. On a fixed strict regular cell, estimate the endpoint Jacobian with Hong--Li finite perturbations; near zero coordinates or branch and basis ties, retain primitive-set inversion.

estimand_functional: \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=s-\prod_{c\in\mathcal C_G}(\mathcal P_c^+\cup\mathcal P_c^-)\) on the joint-margin-preserving nonsingular Gaussian completion family

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The true vector belongs to the polytope formed by the individual and pairwise difference bounds.
The conditional identified set is obtained by slicing the reported joint set at a fixed effect value.
Assumption 4 restricts bias ratios conditionally through ratios of short-minus-supershort coefficient changes.
The reported nonparametric treatment-effect bounds are the tightest possible given the observed assignment, treatment, and response distribution.
Rationalizability is equivalent to membership of observed choice probabilities in a finite generated cone.
Compatibility is characterized by finitely many inequalities and computationally efficient inclusion checks.
Calibrated projection confidence intervals control asymptotic coverage uniformly over a large class of data-generating processes.
With a Gaussian limit, ordinary bootstrap consistency requires full differentiability of the transformation.
Numerical directional differentiation yields consistent inference for directionally differentiable maps under an appropriate step-size sequence.
Joint-test inversion gives identification-robust simultaneous confidence sets for finitely many parameter ratios.
Observed explanatory-power restrictions yield sharp single-setting OVB bounds for broad causal functionals.

tldr: Positive bounded ratios of omitted-variable biases do more than bound pairwise bias differences: on every connected setting graph they force one globally compatible, common-sign bias vector, with the all-zero vector as a closure face. The sharp effect set is therefore the affine image of a product of two-polyhedron unions, not the single bias-difference polytope in HuntingtonKlein2026, Proposition 4 on p. 13. The paper proves both inclusions and exhibits a joint-margin-preserving Gaussian latent-control augmentation for every feasible bias vector; arbitrary observed laws receive containment only, while reverse attainment is confined to the nonsingular jointly Gaussian family with unrestricted admissible cross-setting covariance. It also derives closure-complete log-cycle and Farkas certificates, gives equivalent branch-LP and zero-safe MILP computations including an exact fixed-zero rational check, proves a symbolic support gap, and solves a three-setting equality cycle with two simultaneous pins and an exact \(a/2\) outer-slice gap. For estimated supershort calibration it defines a componentwise undivided polynomial sensitivity region. Total regularized primitive-moment inversion supplies supporting uniform coverage at exact-zero and \(n^{-1/2}\)-weak coefficient changes, while a headline regular-cell theorem gives a stable \(C^1\) endpoint map, its Gaussian limit, consistent Hong--Li numerical derivatives, and pointwise first-order equivalence to the known-cell oracle. The genuinely open frontier is a single data-dependent procedure that combines singular-sequence uniform validity with this pointwise oracle recovery.

project_justification.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026, Assumption 3 on pp. 8--9, imposes positive cross-setting bias ratios with intervals containing one, while Proposition 4 on p. 13 reports a polytope built from separately extremized bias differences and Definition 3 on p. 15 pins that outer set. The paper does not prove equality or converse attainment, and Assumption 4 on pp. 17--18 uses divided supershort ratios without sampling inference at weak denominators.
project_justification.niche: Applied researchers need the exact joint set generated by one latent bias vector, certificates that distinguish genuine incompatibility from a numerical artifact, exact answers after several effects are pinned, and confidence sets that remain valid when the data do not identify a supershort ratio.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an if-and-only-if componentwise sign union with a joint-margin-preserving Gaussian latent augmentation, exact primal--dual computation including fixed-zero strata, analytic support and pin gaps from the published outer polytope, and a solved three-setting cycle. For the undivided supershort sensitivity region, primitive inversion is retained as a supporting uniform-coverage lemma and a separate regular-cell theorem derives endpoint differentiability, a Gaussian limit, consistent numerical derivatives, and pointwise known-cell oracle equivalence. A single procedure that adapts between these regimes remains the first-class open problem.

related_work: HuntingtonKlein2026 is the theorem-level comparator. Assumption 3 on pp. 8--9 imposes bounded positive bias ratios with \(\ell_{jk}\le1\le u_{jk}\), and Proposition 4 on p. 13 gives membership in the resulting pairwise bias-difference polytope. Theorem 1 identifies the exact componentwise sign union and proves converse attainment only on the stated nonsingular jointly Gaussian observed-law family with unrestricted admissible cross-setting covariance, while arbitrary observed laws retain containment. The project-maintained generalization permits calibrated ratio intervals that need not contain one. Theorem 3 proves strict tightening of the published outer polytope throughout its stated symmetric family \(a>0\), \(R>1\), and Theorems 4--5 show that slicing as in Definition 3 on p. 15 can overstate a pinned endpoint by exactly \(a/2\). Assumption 4 on pp. 17--18 motivates, but does not state, the project-maintained componentwise polynomial supershort region; Lemma 2 gives its exhaustive zero-coordinate interpretation. BalkePearl1997 informs the converse-attainment standard. ChernozhukovEtAl2026 supplies the single-setting OVB decomposition and efficient estimation of observed sensitivity components, but does not impose cross-setting ratio closure. CinelliHazlett2020 and Oster2019 motivate the observable benchmarking primitives used by supershort calibration. KitamuraStoye2018 informs the finite primal--dual compatibility architecture, and GalichonHenry2011 informs finite separating inequalities; neither studies a positive-OVB-ratio sign union or its zero closure. KaidoMolinariStoye2019 informs repeated feasibility inversion for projected partially identified parameters; Lemmas 3--4 isolate the standard probabilistic work as fixed-dimensional primitive coverage, covariance consistency, and regularized Slutsky equivalence, with deterministic union inclusion thereafter. FangSantos2019 explains the failure of ordinary bootstrap inference at branch or basis ties. HongLi2018 informs the finite-perturbation derivative in Theorem 6, which instead proves pointwise regular-cell basis stability, differentiability, a Gaussian endpoint law, and first-order equality with the known-cell oracle. BolducKhalafYelou2010 and Dufour1997 explain why divided-ratio Wald inference is unsuitable near zero. AndrewsMikusheva2016 informs the open goal of combining weak-regime validity with strong-regime precision in one data-dependent procedure. These method ancestors do not contain the sharp OVB closure or the stated regular-cell endpoint theorem.
technical_internal_limitation: The joint-margin-preserving Gaussian augmentation proves that no uniformly tighter set follows from the stated sensitivity restrictions over the nonsingular jointly Gaussian residualized observed-law family. It does not assert that every arbitrary non-Gaussian observed law admits every feasible long coefficient; universal algebraic containment holds, while pointwise sharp equality is confined to the stated Gaussian family.
honest_scope: The theorem claims cover the exact componentwise union, its joint-margin-preserving Gaussian attainment, cycle and Farkas certificates, zero-safe branch-LP or MILP equivalence, symbolic support and pin gaps, the solved three-setting equality cycle, and pointwise regular-cell endpoint oracle recovery. Arbitrary observed laws receive containment only; reverse attainment is confined to the stated nonsingular jointly Gaussian observed-law family with unrestricted admissible cross-setting covariance. The supershort object is a calibrated sensitivity region, not a claimed causal identified set. Uniform primitive inversion is a supporting consequence of primitive-ellipsoid coverage and deterministic union inclusion, not a substantive inversion theorem. One data-dependent procedure that is uniformly valid on singular sequences and oracle-equivalent off them remains open. The attainment sanity reduction holds coordinatewise: for \(B_i\ne0\), the structural equation collapses identically to \(Y_i=s_iD_i+U_i\) and leaves the observed vector untouched, while for \(B_i=0\) it collapses to the ordinary short regression with an independent latent control. Singleton graph components recover the Cartesian product of the published individual OVB intervals, \(R=1\) in the symmetric two-setting family forces equal biases and makes the support gap zero, and away from zero denominators the polynomial supershort restriction reduces to the reciprocal-ratio interval.

literature_map: HuntingtonKlein2026 is the direct anchor. Assumption 3 on pp. 8--9 states \(B^j=\rho^{jk}B^k\) with \(0<\ell_{jk}\le1\le u_{jk}\) and discusses the common-sign and zero-bias implications. Proposition 4 on p. 13 gives only containment of the \(K\)-setting effect vector in a pairwise bias-difference polytope, and Definition 3 on p. 15 performs pinning in that outer set. Assumption 4 on pp. 17--18 restricts ratios conditionally through divided supershort coefficient changes. No converse-attainment theorem, componentwise polynomial supershort closure, or sampling-inference theorem appears. The generalized ratio intervals not required to contain one and the undivided polynomial branches in this core are project-maintained novel constructions, not standard Huntington--Klein conditions. BalkePearl1997, Sections 2--3, supplies the latent-response linear-programming and endpoint-attainment pattern. KitamuraStoye2018, Theorem 3.1 and Section 4, supplies the primal finite-cone representation and its dual half-space logic, including equality faces; positive ratios instead create a union of sign polyhedra whose logarithmic representation omits the zero stratum. GalichonHenry2011, Theorems 1--3, supplies finite compatibility inequalities and dual separation. KaidoMolinariStoye2019, Sections 2--3 and Theorem 3.1, supplies calibrated projection with uniform coverage for finite moment models; the present supporting lemmas make the covariance inverse total and explicitly separate probabilistic primitive coverage from deterministic union inclusion. FangSantos2019, Theorem 3.1 and Section 3, establishes ordinary-bootstrap failure at merely directionally differentiable maps. HongLi2018, Section 3, supplies finite-perturbation numerical differentiation; Theorem 6 specializes that device to a locally fixed supershort sign branch and primal--dual basis, derives the \(C^1\) endpoint Jacobian and Gaussian limit, and proves pointwise first-order agreement with the known-cell oracle. BolducKhalafYelou2010, Sections 2--3, inverts joint tests for numerator--denominator primitives, and Dufour1997, Theorems 3.1--3.3, rules out uniformly valid always-bounded inference near ratio nonidentification. ChernozhukovEtAl2026, Theorems 2--4, gives sharp single-setting omitted-variable-bias bounds and efficient estimation of observed bound components, but has no cross-setting multiplicative closure.

novelty_justification.published_axis: The closest result is HuntingtonKlein2026, Proposition 4 on p. 13. It proves only that the effect vector belongs to a polytope built from separately extremized bias differences, even though Assumption 3 on pp. 8--9 requires one positive-ratio bias vector and notes the induced common sign and transitivity. Theorem 1 gives the affine image of one positive or negative polyhedron per connected component and adds a joint-margin-preserving observationally equivalent Gaussian augmentation; equality is claimed only on that nonsingular Gaussian family, while arbitrary laws retain containment. Theorem 3 gives a symbolic strict support gap on every \(a>0\), \(R>1\) in its two-setting family; Theorem 4 gives an exact pin gap; and Theorem 5 solves a three-setting equality cycle with a zero stratum and two simultaneous pins. Definition 3 on p. 15 contains none of these slice characterizations. Assumption 4 on pp. 17--18 motivates the project-maintained polynomial sensitivity region. Theorem 6 adds a separate pointwise regular-cell result: stable winning branches and primal--dual bases make its directional endpoint map \(C^1\), yield a Gaussian limit, and make Hong--Li numerical-delta endpoint intervals first-order equivalent to the known-cell oracle. ChernozhukovEtAl2026 is the nearest OVB sharpness and efficiency paper, but its target is a single-setting bound and it imposes no cross-setting multiplicative compatibility. KitamuraStoye2018 and GalichonHenry2011 contribute transferable primal--dual compatibility methods, not an OVB sign-union theorem. KaidoMolinariStoye2019, FangSantos2019, HongLi2018, and BolducKhalafYelou2010 separately cover projection, directional maps, numerical derivatives, and ratios; none states this multi-setting closure or regular-cell endpoint result.
novelty_justification.repo_axis: The closest archived proposals contribute reusable proof motifs but no result on Huntington--Klein or multi-setting OVB ratios. The accepted partial-transport run supplies full-law endpoint attainment; the collider-bias run identifies open-set separation from rectangular relaxations; the BudgetIV run records unresolved exact cycle and weak-ratio topology; and the data-fusion run leaves tie-uniform numerical-delta inference open. This core does not treat those claims as proved. It instantiates their missing common-witness lesson at a new published target and makes the exact sign closure, strict support gap, and undivided supershort relation explicit.
